Answer: C
Reason: The axial CT image demonstrates a well-circumscribed anterior mediastinal mass with a distinct, thick calcified rim and internal heterogeneous density (including fat/soft tissue), which is the classic radiological appearance of a mature teratoma. While the patient has a history of breast cancer, the specific morphological features of calcification and mixed composition strongly favor a benign teratoma over metastasis or other mediastinal masses.
